about.title: Sonora Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member changes everything, and the paperwork that follows can feel impossible from a kitchen table in Sonora. A wrongful death claim is the civil side of that loss: a way for a spouse, domestic partner, or children (and in some cases other dependents or heirs) to ask the responsible party to account for what was taken. It runs on its own track, apart from any criminal charges the Tuolumne County District Attorney may or may not bring. Public records for 2025 list 45 injury collisions and 52 people hurt in Sonora, with no traffic deaths recorded that year. Wrongful death cases here still arise—from crashes along Rt 49 or Mono Way, from falls, from care that fell short, from products that failed. California gives most families two years from the date of death to file, and far less time when a city, county, or state agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Sonora families, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death action, starting with the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can tell you quickly where your family fits.

items.title: The Clock Is Real
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window shrinks sharply when a public entity is involved. Connecting early protects options you may not know you have.

items.title: Every Loss Counted
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Sonora recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Are wrongful death claims still filed here?
items.answer: Yes. Traffic fatalities are only one source of these cases, and a single year with none recorded does not mean families in Tuolumne County are never affected. Deaths tied to falls, medical or nursing care, defective products, and workplace incidents also give rise to claims. The legal standards are the same regardless of how the loss occurred.

items.question: Do we have to wait for a criminal case to finish before filing?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves independently of any criminal prosecution. The two can proceed at the same time, and a civil claim can go forward even if no charges are ever filed. What matters is meeting the civil deadline, which runs from the date of death.

items.question: What if a government vehicle or public road condition was involved?
items.answer: Claims against a city, county, or state agency follow a much shorter timeline than the standard two years, and they usually require a formal claim before a lawsuit can be filed. Missing that early step can close the door on the case. If you suspect a public entity had any role, it is worth speaking with an attorney right away.
